prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and for the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: The Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall proposal and the Z2 classification introduced a new organizing principle for electronic band structures: topology protected by time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling, with robust helical edge and surface states. The idea was tested against nature quickly and decisively by Molenkamp's HgTe/CdTe transport measurements, and later by ARPES and transport in many material families. It has redirected materials searches, spin-orbit physics and spintronics for almost two decades, and the experimental confirmation is broad rather than a single result. In this shortlist it is the clearest case of a theoretical concept, an experimental realisation and a lasting field-wide consequence in one package, and the three credited names map onto it without padding. Opening support places it first for two members and in the top four for four, so it is not a one-voice candidate.
statement.case_against: The attribution is genuinely contested. The HgTe quantum well proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang was what made the Molenkamp experiment possible, Shoucheng Zhang is deceased and cannot be honoured, and the 3D generalisation (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan's experiments) is outside this credit set, so a citation centred on the 2D effect risks looking narrow. The 2016 prize for topological phases of matter will also lead some colleagues to see this as overlapping, even though it covered topological phase transitions and Haldane-type phases rather than time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators. If the committee cannot settle those allocations, B035 is the cleaner proposal on credit, and I would not defend B008 against a well-argued shift to it.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's realisation took atomic timekeeping to the 1e-18 level, with a clean two-person credit and good timing given the possible redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree that B035 is the best-credited candidate on the table and I ranked it lower mainly out of unfamiliarity with the field, not on scientific grounds. Where I differ is on novelty: the prize has already recognised the frequency comb in 2005 and ion-clock work in 2012, so the committee must be able to say what is new in the lattice clock rather than treat it as the next increment in a recognised line. Your own uncertainty about Ye being framed around clocks versus the broader comb and ultracold programme matters for the citation. If the committee settles on a narrowly worded citation naming the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation, I would support B035 as a serious alternative to B008 rather than a lesser choice.

responses.point: Johansson ranked circuit QED first and described it as an original, widely reproduced architecture distinct from the 2025 macroscopic quantum tunnelling prize, while flagging his own field bias and the omission of Girvin from the theory credit.
responses.response: I recognise the technological weight of B004, and as Chair of the 2025 cycle I am cautious about calling it independent of that prize. The 2025 award concerned macroscopic quantum effects in circuits, and circuit QED builds directly on those devices, so a second superconducting-circuit prize within two years needs a justification a layperson would accept as a separate discovery. The theory credit is also thinner than the experimental one: Girvin and Huang were part of the 2004 proposal. You also noted that you are close to this field, which I take as a fair disclosure. I would keep B004 as an alternative, but I would not elevate it above B008 or B035 this year.

responses.point: Mehlig also placed topological insulators first, arguing the area is conceptually new, confirmed across HgTe, InAs/GaSb and 3D materials, and that recognition is timely given the 2016 prize was more general.
responses.response: I agree on merit and on maturity. Where I would qualify your framing is the attribution: calling the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp triple coherent is true of the three names supplied, but it does not remove the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, which you also flagged. I think we should be explicit that the citation rests on the prediction of the effect and the Z2 invariant plus the first observation, not on every later materials step, and that the 3D class is a consequence of the same idea rather than a separately credited achievement. I would be uneasy if our support for B008 depended on skipping that conversation.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked the Higgs experimental discovery first and topological insulators second, noting that the 2013 theory prize leaves the experimental half unrecognised, while accepting that credit among ATLAS and CMS leaders is unresolved.
responses.response: The scientific significance of B006 is not in doubt and I do not discount it because I work in a different field. My difficulty is the same as yours: any three names for two collaborations of thousands are a proxy, and the supplied credit set differs among members on Della Negra, Virdee and Gianotti. A prize built on that choice would be contested from the day it was announced. Unless the committee can agree a principled rule for which leaders are credited, I find it harder to support B006 this year than B008, although I would welcome a well-argued configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the credit for HgTe (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and the 3D topological insulator work can be handled by the citation wording within three names.
Whether the 2016 prize for topological phases of matter is judged to overlap too closely with the Z2 topological insulator.
Whether B035 offers a cleaner two-person credit that most members would prefer to a contested three-person B008 once the opening-ballot support is considered.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My own work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism is adjacent to B008 and B051, which may bias me toward them, but I have no documented personal or institutional connection to any credited candidate.
